Retrieved 2026-09-07 by the whole-corpus sweep of the 9,890 McGill student
publication items (p_479). "Kanawana" occurs once in the issue.

The OCR renders Y.M.C.A. as "T.M.C.A." throughout, which is the scanner
misreading the Y, and "Laure.ntians" for Laurentians. Both are transcribed as
printed below; nothing else in the passage is ambiguous.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
THE REPORT, TRANSCRIBED IN FULL
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

BIBLE STUDY SUPPER WAS HELD YESTERDAY
Mr. Bradford Spoke on Boys' Work in Canada.

The Y. M. Bible Study Groups met as usual last night, In Strathcona Hall.
Supper was served shortly after 6 o'clock, under the chairmanship of "Art"
Walsh, Med. '21. The fellows, as usual, did full justice to the good things set
before them. At 6.45 the groups separated to their respective meeting places
upstairs, under the regular teachers.

The Senior Class continue to have their Interesting social service topics under
the leadership of Mr. John Bradford, of Central T.M.C.A. Mr. Pierce, Editor of
the "Locomotive Engineer," who was advertised to speak to thpm last night, was
unable to put In an appearance, owing to Illness. It Is expected, however, that
he can come next Monday night.

Mr. Bradford himself favoured the group with an Interesting description of the
most recent developments In "Boys' Work in Canada." This new work Is known to
most of us now, at least by name, as the Canadian Standard Efficiency Test. This
takes the form of a definite programme concerning every phase of the normal
boy's activity. It contemplates the development of a new type of Christian
leadership. Its plan of work is four-fold, Its divisions being: 1, Mental; 2,
Physical; 3, Spiritual, and 4, Social. Among its other good points Is the
emphasizing of the value of school training for life. The Importance of habits
of observation In the ordinary walks of life Is also laid stress on. Training
for leadership among boys is the chief point on the Social side. Under the head
of Religion they group Poetry, Music, Art and Nature, as well as what we usually
connect with religious activities.

Although begun In Canada, the Idea is being taken up rapidly In the United
States by Churches, Sunday School Associations and the T.M.C.A. Mr. Bradford
considers it one of the most sensible and hopeful ideas yet tried in the
training of the adolescent for sane, Christian manhood. In conclusion he asked
"Doc." Busby to give his point of view. The latter told about the valuable work
along this line being done at the Kanawana Boys' Camp In the Laurentians.

As there will be only two more sessions of the Bible Study Groups this year it
is hoped the attendance will keep up to normal.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WHY THIS MATTERS, CHECKED AGAINST THE DESTINATION BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. IT IS THE DOCUMENT wiki/connections/institutional-lineage/wallace-forgie.md
   SAYS DOES NOT EXIST. That article, written 2026-09-07, has a section headed
   "Kanawana's stake in any of this" which begins "Indirect, and worth stating
   plainly rather than overclaiming" and argues from the general -- "Kanawana
   ran a YMCA boys' programme through the decades when CSET was the national
   framework for exactly that." It had no document connecting the camp to the
   programme. This is one, and it is early: 25 February 1918, five months
   before the October 1918 date the CSET's own board gives. Note what it is and
   is not. It is a student paper reporting a speaker at a McGill YMCA supper
   saying that work "along this line" was being done at Kanawana. It is not the
   camp's own record, and "along this line" is the reporter's phrase for a
   connection the speaker drew. What it establishes is that in February 1918
   people in Montreal YMCA circles understood Kanawana's work as CSET work and
   said so out loud to a room of university students.

2. IT IS ALSO A BIOGRAPHY FOR A NAME THE WIKI HOLDS AS ONE LINE. John Bradford
   appears in wiki/people/directors-index.md only as one of two men who
   supervised the camp in 1917 alongside Jos. Dalley, under MacKinnon. Here he
   is, seven months later, "of Central Y.M.C.A.", running the senior social
   service class of McGill's Bible Study Groups through a term, and standing up
   as Montreal's exponent of the Canadian Standard Efficiency Test. The man who
   ran the camp in the summer was teaching its method to undergraduates in the
   winter.

3. A CONTEMPORARY DESCRIPTION OF CSET, FROM OUTSIDE ITS OWN LITERATURE. The
   fourfold divisions are given as "1, Mental; 2, Physical; 3, Spiritual, and 4,
   Social" -- not in the order of Luke 2:52 (wisdom, stature, favour with God,
   favour with man), which is how the programme's own board describes its
   origin. And the religion heading is described as grouping "Poetry, Music, Art
   and Nature, as well as what we usually connect with religious activities."
   That last clause is worth keeping: a camp in the Laurentians running a
   programme whose religious category formally includes Nature is a different
   thing from one where nature study is recreation.

4. "ALTHOUGH BEGUN IN CANADA, THE IDEA IS BEING TAKEN UP RAPIDLY IN THE UNITED
   STATES." A dated, contemporaneous statement of the programme's spread south,
   from February 1918, made by a man in a position to know.

5. "DOC." BUSBY IS A NEW NAME AND OCCURS NOWHERE ELSE IN THIS PROJECT (greped
   across wiki/, kb/facts.json and project-docs/ before this was written: zero
   hits). He is at a McGill Bible study supper, he is called "Doc.", and he is
   the person in the room who could speak to what Kanawana did. That is a
   camp connection of some kind and it is entirely undocumented here. The
   quotation marks around "Doc." in the original suggest a nickname rather than
   a title, which is a caution for any search that assumes a physician.

NULL RESULTS IN THIS ISSUE. "Kanawana" occurs once, in this report. The rest of
the issue is McGill student news; the adjoining column advertises the Class of
Medicine '21's production of "The Coronation of King Cook III".
